text: Multi-session benchmark: does the idea graph help when context is reset between sessions?
description:
Follow-up to the graph-grounding benchmark (8ac03697), whose v1–v3 runs were a valid null: single-session synthetic tasks hit a ceiling in both conditions. Its own lesson: test only where durable context is genuinely needed across sessions.

Setup idea: multi-session tasks with a context reset between sessions, where decisions made in session 2 constrain session 5. Two candidate task sources:
- SWE-EVO / SWE-Milestone as-is (cheap to adopt; not designed with an idea graph in mind). MemTrace (arXiv 2610.04838) reports its largest gains exactly there (+17.8 on SWE-Milestone).
- Replay a stretch of this repo's own history as a sequence of sessions (closer to what Aimparency claims; scoring is harder). Score completion, rework, and contradictions with earlier decisions.

Process: design the experiment fully (pre-registered tasks and pass criteria) before building anything.

status.comment: Felix (2026-10-17): interesting, no decision yet. Open: which task source (SWE-EVO/SWE-Milestone vs. replaying this repo's history), and whether to spend the effort now.
